article.title: NFL EDGE Sunday Morning Brief
article.dek: Lamar Jackson is officially out for Sunday night with Tyler Huntley starting, two of the three headline cards changed overnight, and rain is bearing down on three of the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoffs.

items.headline: Lamar Jackson is out; Tyler Huntley starts Sunday night
paragraphs: Baltimore ruled Lamar Jackson (ankle) out Friday, and head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Tyler “Snoop” Huntley starts against the Falcons in Atlanta — 8:20 p.m. ET Sunday night. Huntley went 8-of-9 in relief last week but the offense produced no points across five drives, and the Ravens are 6-11 without Jackson since 2019. The line is hurting too: center Cam Jurgens (concussion) is out, edge rusher Trey Hendrickson is out, and Zay Flowers, Marlon Humphrey and Andrew Vorhees are questionable.

The market has already digested it. Atlanta sat at -3.0 on DraftKings all evening and -3.5 on FanDuel — the number moved when the Huntley news hit, then stopped. The news is in the price now. If your book's line differs from that, tap Check: type in the line and price you can actually bet and the app re-runs it through the model and the evaluator for a verdict on YOUR number.
items.takeaway: The news is in the price. Your edge is the number in front of you.

items.headline: Quarterback check: no stale numbers on the board
paragraphs: The app's quarterback feed is fresh and matches the news. Tyson Bagent starts for Chicago at Green Bay with Caleb Williams (hamstring) out a third straight game — Williams practiced on a limited basis Friday. Jameis Winston starts for the Giants while Jayden Daniels (elbow) is expected to suit up for Washington. Kyler Murray is listed as Minnesota's starter at New Orleans, with Jacoby Brissett starting for Arizona. Tyler Huntley for Baltimore, as above.
That's the check that matters on a Sunday morning: when the board agrees with the news, there's no stale number to fade and no rumor to chase. Bet the slate, not the rumor.
items.takeaway: The board's quarterbacks match the news. Nothing to fade, nothing to chase.

items.headline: Injury roundup, grouped
paragraphs: New England put leading receiver Mack Hollins (calf) on injured reserve Saturday — 15 catches for 209 yards, out at least four games. A.J. Brown (ankle) was already on IR, fullback Reggie Gilliam joined them, and the Patriots ruled out both starting cornerbacks, Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis III, for Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET game against Las Vegas. Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is out for Philadelphia's London game against Jacksonville at 9:30 a.m. ET. Ja'Marr Chase (concussion protocol) is trending toward playing for Cincinnati; Tee Higgins is still to be decided. San Francisco is without Nick Bosa for a third straight game.

Friday's outs still stand: Breece Hall (quad) for the Jets; Mason Graham, Mike Hall Jr., Teven Jenkins, Tylan Wallace and Carsen Ryan for Cleveland; Kaden Elliss and Anfernee Jennings for New Orleans; Christian Darrisaw for Minnesota; Amani Hooker for Tennessee; Tank Dell for Houston. Terry McLaurin (hamstring) is a game-time decision. Final inactives land about 90 minutes before each kickoff — this brief can't have them, so watch that window.
items.takeaway: Questionable is not out and out is not questionable. Plan around the outs; check the rest at the inactive deadline.

items.headline: Sunday weather: three wet 1:00 p.m. ET games
paragraphs: The National Weather Service has rain at 100% for three of the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoffs: Landover (Giants at Commanders) — rain showers then thunderstorms likely, near 70, east wind 9-15 mph; Pittsburgh (Colts at Steelers) — rain showers, 63, gusts to 26; East Rutherford (Browns at Jets) — rain after 8 a.m., 64, gusts to 25. Foxborough (Raiders at Patriots) has a 40% shower chance after 4 p.m. Green Bay (Bears at Packers) is sunny and 79; Miami (Bengals at Dolphins) is 91 with a slight storm chance after 3 p.m.; Seattle (49ers at Seahawks, 4:25 p.m. ET) is sunny and 59.
File the weather, don't force it into a totals opinion — rain is a fact, the total is a market. If the rain has you eyeing a number, run it through Check with your book's line and price.
items.takeaway: Three 1:00 p.m. ET games look genuinely wet. Know it before you bet it.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Hit Rate is on the Broncos — and it changed overnight
paragraphs: Hit Rate means the supported pick the app thinks is most likely to win — win probability first, value second. The app's own tutorial says Hit Rate ≠ Profit Rate. This morning it's Denver on the moneyline at -180 on FanDuel, visiting the Chargers at 4:05 p.m. ET. The app evaluates Denver's chance at 66.5% against a 64.3% breakeven at that price — a thin positive edge, reliability MEDIUM.

Denver is a 3.5-point road favorite in the market, so this isn't a contrarian stance — it's the likeliest winner on the board per the app. If your book has Denver cheaper than -180, that's better than the card; if it's pricier, tap Check and run your price before you decide.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate chases the win, not the value. Denver is the app's likeliest winner today.

items.headline: Balanced stayed on Minnesota; Value flipped to San Francisco
paragraphs: Balanced is the middle ground — a strong pick without paying too much, a good starting point for a new bettor. It's Minnesota on the moneyline at -130 on DraftKings (1:00 p.m. ET at New Orleans), the same card and price as last night. The app's model gives the Vikings 69.4% against a 55.3% market-implied chance — but note the LOW reliability tag. Middle ground means middling conviction.

Value is always the model's +EV play, and it re-dealt overnight: San Francisco -3 on FanDuel in the 4:25 p.m. ET game at Seattle. The model gives the cover a 50.5% chance against 46.9% implied — a 1.6% edge, reliability MEDIUM. Last night Value was the Raiders +3.5; if you played that number, that's yesterday's play.
items.takeaway: Same team can sit on two cards for two different reasons. Play the card, not the team.

items.headline: How to use today's news inside the app
paragraphs: Every news item above closes the loop the same way. The board refreshes every morning and evening. When a line moved on news the board hasn't priced yet — or your book isn't DraftKings or FanDuel — tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and returns a bet/no-bet verdict on your price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.

One mechanics note: -180 means every $1.80 you risk wins $1; -130 means every $1.30 risks to win $1. That's price mechanics, not a stake — the app sizes your actual stake from your bankroll and your staking setting, which is deliberately conservative.
items.takeaway: Report the news first, then use it: Check is how news becomes a number.

items.headline: Handle vs. tickets — the two numbers inside every split
paragraphs: Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: imagine a split screen showing 70% of the tickets (BET) on Team A but only 40% of the money (HND) on Team A. That means lots of small bets on Team A and fewer, bigger bets on Team B. Tickets count the number of bets; handle counts the dollars.

A gap between the two is called a tickets-vs-handle disagreement, and it's the starting point of every “respect the money” conversation — not the conclusion. Sharper, price-sensitive bettors often wait for a better number instead of betting early, so the disagreement alone is a question, not an answer. Our rule needs the split plus corroborating line movement or a second book before it becomes a Fade. When a real one qualifies, this section will say so plainly.
items.takeaway: Tickets count the crowd; handle counts the cash. When they disagree, ask why — don't just pick a side.

items.headline: Minnesota keeps getting cheaper
paragraphs: The Vikings' price kept sliding overnight. The DraftKings spread went from -2.5 to -1.5 (now -118), while FanDuel held -1.5 (-120) and Pinnacle sits at -2.0 (-106). The Balanced card still has Minnesota on the moneyline at -130 on DraftKings — the same price as last night — so the pick didn't change, the price did.
If your book is still hanging -2.5 on the Vikings, that's a stale number. Tap Check and see what the evaluator says about it.
items.takeaway: The price moved, the pick didn't. Shop it.

items.headline: The cards rotated overnight
paragraphs: Two of the three headline cards re-dealt. Hit Rate went from Minnesota to Denver (moneyline -180, FanDuel). Value went from the Raiders +3.5 to the 49ers -3 (FanDuel). Balanced stayed on Minnesota at the same -130 on DraftKings.
When the card changes, the play changes — yesterday's numbers are yesterday's. Check your book's number against today's card, not last night's.
items.takeaway: When the card changes, the play changes. Check your book's number.

items.headline: Falcons steady, Steelers split stands, Bears still favored
paragraphs: Atlanta held at -3.0 on DraftKings (-3.5 on FanDuel) all evening after the Huntley news — the market absorbed the Lamar news and stopped moving. Pittsburgh is still -3 on DraftKings and -2.5 on FanDuel, with prices ticking a cent or two. Chicago is still a 1.5-point favorite at Green Bay despite starting the backup — the market isn't flinching at Bagent.
Half points and stale numbers are where Check earns its keep: your book's line is the only line that matters.
items.takeaway: Half points and stale numbers are where Check earns its keep.

items.headline: London first, then the 1:00 p.m. ET wave
paragraphs: Philadelphia and Jacksonville kick off in London at 9:30 a.m. ET — the first prices of the day move first. Shop this morning's card prices now, not after the London game kicks: the 1:00 p.m. ET wave has eight games, and that's where stale numbers go to hide.
Inactives land about 90 minutes before each kickoff, so the window to re-check is real. Shop the price before the game, not during it.
items.takeaway: Shop the price before the game, not during it.

items.headline: Log the losers too
paragraphs: Settlement is manual — the tracker only works if you're honest with yourself. If a card play loses today, log it the same night you placed it. An honest ledger beats a flattering one.
items.takeaway: An honest ledger beats a flattering one.
